neighbours.label: function words in prose on Tibetan, Khmer or Buddhist history ('saints such as', 'the new Khmer king (')
fire: Tantric teachings reached Tibet with Bengali monks such as Tilopa and Marpa.
Angkor was retaken by the young Khmer ruler (Suryavarman II) in 1113.
Buddhist texts came to Tibet with Nepalese scholars such as Shantarakshita.
The Cham were defeated by the old Khmer general (a royal prince) at sea.
The Tibetan empire reached its height in the eighth century under a strong king.
Vajrayana monks in Tibet studied with Indian masters such as Naropa.
The Khmer kingdom was ruled by a line of Hindu kings (the Varmans) for centuries.
A Tibetan thangka was a gift from the emperor to the high lama.
quiet: Cotton mills reached Ohio with Scottish workers such as Thomas and Bell.
Boston was retaken by the young American army (with cannon) in 1776.
Printed books came to Ohio with German families such as the Muellers.
The Dutch were defeated by the old English navy (a royal fleet) at sea.
The Ohio canal reached its height in the nineteenth century under a strong board.
Medical students in Ohio studied with Scottish doctors such as Rush.
The Ohio company was run by a line of Yankee merchants (the Putnams) for decades.
A silver teapot was a gift from the mayor to the new bishop.

notes: Card: ' by' x5, ' the' x4, ' and' x2, ' (' x2, ' King' x2, ' of' x2, in Tibetan, Khmer, Hungarian and tech history. Probe: ' as' in 'Indian saints such as' 0.909; ' (' after 'Khmer king' 0.690; 'with Indian traders' 0.667; 'Khmer army (with' 0.335; Hungarian 'King Bela' 0.127 and 'Stephen' 0.209, so the Hungarian peaks are not covered. Near misses move the same frames to other places.
